concepts.title: Development: Meaning and Principles
concepts.definition: Development is the pattern of orderly, sequential change that continues through life -- gains and losses alike -- from conception to old age. Its principles: development proceeds in definite directions, at individual rates, in interrelated dimensions, and through the joint action of heredity and environment.
concepts.key_idea: Lifelong, orderly and joint-made -- development is change with a pattern, not a race with a finish line.

solution_steps.explain: Development covers organised change across physical, cognitive and socio-emotional dimensions through the whole life span.
Direction, individual rate, interrelation and continuity describe how change unfolds.
Heredity supplies potentials; environment and context decide how they unfold.

concepts.title: Heredity, Environment and Context
concepts.definition: The nature-nurture issue asks how much genes and how much environment shape us. Developmental psychology answers: jointly -- genes set ranges, environments select points within them, and cultural context colours every stage's meaning and timetable.
concepts.key_idea: Genes write in pencil, environment fills the ink -- context decides what each stage means.
concepts.textbook_ref: kepy103.txt influence sections (heredity genes, environment, context and culture, nature nurture interaction)
question_patterns: explain the influence of heredity on human development

solution_steps.explain: Heredity supplies the inherited blueprint -- potentials, temperament, ranges of possibility.
Nutrition, family, schooling and culture realise, restrict or redirect those potentials.
Development is the negotiated product of both, read always within its context.

concepts.title: Stages of the Life Span
concepts.definition: The life span divides into stages -- prenatal, infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood and old age -- each with characteristic physical, cognitive and socio-emotional tasks, from attachment and language in infancy to identity in adolescence and integrity in old age.
concepts.key_idea: One life span, several stages -- each with its own jobs of growth to finish before the next begins.

solution_steps.explain: Prenatal to old age in sequence, with infancy and childhood building attachment, language and thought.
Identity formation, puberty and heightened peer orientation define the stage the reader is in.
Adulthood centres on work and relationships; old age brings integration, wisdom and adjustment to loss.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Two identical twins are raised in different cities and grow into adults with different interests. Explain using heredity-environment interaction.

solution_template.explain: Identical genes give the twins the same potentials and temperamental starting point.
Different schools, peers and city cultures offered different models and opportunities.
One blueprint, two realisations -- development is the joint product, never genes alone.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Match each behaviour to its stage: babbling; identity crisis; retirement planning; first steps.

solution_template.explain: Babbling belongs to infancy; first steps to late infancy or early childhood.
Identity crisis is adolescence's signature search.
Retirement planning belongs to late adulthood's task of adjustment and integrity.
